device: iPhone 18 Pro simulator, iOS 27, dark appearance, default large text

steps.name: Profile
steps.strength: Direct navigation and an appearance choice; no explanatory paragraphs.
steps.issue: No material copy bloat. Fit passport is the only label that needs discovery effort.
steps.accessibility: Observed 60-point navigation rows and 44-point appearance targets; VoiceOver not tested.
steps.recommendation: Keep the structure. Consider Measurements if the destination is simplified to that task.

steps.name: Closets
steps.strength: One name field and one action; empty state is brief.
steps.issue: NEW CLOSET NAME can be shortened to Closet name; no material explanatory bloat in the empty state.
steps.accessibility: Placeholder is faint and vanishes after entry; a persistent accessible field name should remain.
steps.limits: No custom closet was present; populated membership and delete controls were reviewed in source only.
steps.recommendation: Keep the screen simple. Use Closet name; avoid adding a tutorial to fill the blank space.

steps.name: Fit passport / sizing
steps.strength: Optional extra measurements are collapsed; units and individual field labels are useful.
steps.issue: The intro narrates two different tasks; OPTIONAL is repeated five times, then Optional details adds a sixth label. Size comparison is an entire second form on the same page. The chart repeats REMOVE SIZE for every blank row; defaults present three empty sizes before there is a comparison task. PRIVATE BY DEFAULT introduces a long footer about AI requests and medical assessments in a measurements task.
steps.accessibility: Long low-contrast monospaced instructions are hard to scan. Field frames in the AX tree are small; real touch/focus and large text still need testing.
steps.recommendation: Lead with Measurements. Say All fields optional once. Move measuring tips into How to measure and make Compare a size chart a separate action. Start the chart with one size row, and put remove actions on each row without repeating a large text action. Replace the privacy block with Saved on this device. Not sent with AI photos. Put Sizing varies by brand beside the comparison result; remove the unsolicited medical framing.
steps.sourceFinding: CONFIDENCE percentage is generated by a hand-written range/count formula, not a calibrated probability. Result state not rendered.

steps.name: Item detail
steps.strength: Large garment image and visible identification code.
steps.issue: SH-001 appears in the title and again below the image. ORIGINAL ONLY sits above a USE ORIGINAL switch even though no cutout exists. DETAIL repeats the page's purpose. Image controls occupy the first screen while the garment name and useful actions do not. WORN 0 TIMES and LAST WORN NEVER say the same thing on two lines. DELETE ITEM is a full-sized button beside everyday actions.
steps.accessibility: The original-image switch offers an unclear state when only one image exists; repeated code adds reading noise. Edit pickers show only their selected values (FOOTWEAR, SNEAKERS, BLACK); do not remove their accessible names when cleaning copy.
steps.recommendation: Keep one visible code and show the garment name. Move Original/Cutout and Improve cutout into Edit photo; show a cutout failure only when it affects the current action. Hide empty wear history, or show Not worn yet once. Keep real wear data. Put Delete in an overflow menu and retain its confirmation.

steps.name: Add Piece
steps.strength: Photo sources use clear verbs. Debug-only Demo image is correctly excluded from release source.
steps.issue: A three-step progress banner presents automatic cleanup as a user task, although the flow is a single scrolling sheet. Four equal buttons plus DROP IMAGE compete for attention in Debug. Failure state says ORIGINAL ONLY, BACKGROUND REMOVAL FAILED — RETRY, and SAVE ORIGINAL across the same screen. The form uses database headings IDENTITY, CLASSIFICATION, ORGANIZATION; DISPLAY NAME is needlessly technical; NOTES is printed twice. AUTO-SUGGESTED · REVIEW BEFORE SAVING spans a full line. Tags explains comma syntax in its label.
steps.accessibility: The numbered circles repeat the stage labels; the combined Step N of 3 accessibility label should remain if the indicator remains.
steps.recommendation: Use two main choices: Take photo and Choose photo. Put Files under another-source menu, keep demo tools out of release, and treat cleanup as inline progress rather than a full step. Use one message: Couldn’t remove the background. You can save the original. Provide Retry and Save piece. Keep image rotation as compact tools. Show Name, Brand, Size, Type, Color directly. Rename subtype Type. Collapse Tags/Notes into More details. Say Suggested beside inferred values and keep one Notes label. Make tag entry chips instead of exposing comma parsing.
steps.limits: Observed a local cutout failure with an unsaved Debug demo fixture. AI de-wrinkle was hidden in this build; its upload disclosure was reviewed in source only.

steps.name: Saved Fits and suggestions
steps.strength: Saved fits remain image-led and the resume action is clear.
steps.issue: Your draft is saved on this device explains routine persistence under Continue your fit. Every tile displays WORN 0×. For you is immediately explained by New combinations from your closet. Suggestions repeat origin in New combinations from your closet, ...from pieces you already own, and FROM YOUR CLOSET. SOFT STRUCTURE, CITY LAYERS, and WEEKEND MODE are preset editorial names with little identifying value.
steps.accessibility: Garment collage is backed by a combined fit label. Zero wear counts add spoken detail without helping choose a fit.
steps.recommendation: Use Continue fit alone, or a small Draft label. Hide zero counts. Rename For you to Suggestions so no explainer is needed. Keep the suggestion feature, but show the outfit plus one factual caption (Black + white) and Save fit. Remove the repeated origin chip and the prose describing colors already visible.

steps.name: Saved Fit detail
steps.strength: Flat-lay image, garment names, and garment codes are useful.
steps.issue: Fit-level WORN 0× plus WORN 0 on every garment repeat empty history. The garment list consumes space without bringing everyday actions forward. Lower page repeats FIT WORN 0 and stacks Try on me, Mark worn today, Duplicate fit, Share fit, Delete fit with almost equal button treatment.
steps.accessibility: Codes and names should remain; the same wear fact need not be announced for every row.
steps.recommendation: Show wear history once for the fit, with item history available on demand. Hide zero counts. Put Wear today and Edit near the fit preview. Use Wear today consistently on both item and fit pages. Keep Share in the toolbar; put Duplicate/Delete in overflow. Show edit fields after Edit rather than as permanent empty forms.

steps.name: Try On
steps.strength: Photo quality instructions support getting a usable reference; garment selection has a visible six-piece limit.
steps.issue: YOUR CLOTHES. YOUR PERSPECTIVE. is a slogan. START WITH YOU adds another heading before the photo instructions and CHOOSE YOUR PHOTO. WHAT WOULD YOU LIKE TO TRY? is a long substitute for Pieces. TRY ON · 1 TRY-ON repeats its own action. The live build opens the entire preparation form and only says Try-on is coming soon after the garment list. It still offers photo inputs and a disabled generation button, plus SAVED PREVIEWS · 0. Privacy sheet is a dense continuous monospaced block; selected-only uploads and on-device saves are explained more than once. Empty Saved previews adds even when your allowance runs out to a basic empty state.
steps.accessibility: Pants / skirt wraps into two lines despite regular text size; repeated marketing headings add reading noise. Privacy copy is legible but the long unbroken paragraphs raise reading effort. VoiceOver order and large text were not exercised.
steps.recommendation: Use Your photo, Choose photo, Pieces, and Generate preview. Keep one short photo instruction with expanded photo tips available on demand. Remove the slogan. Check availability before showing the task. Hide the Try On entry when unavailable and no previews exist; retain access to saved previews when they exist. Keep the visual-preview limitation at generation/result, rather than repeating it in normal wardrobe screens. Keep consent and provider-specific retention information. Group it into short statements for what is sent, who processes it, retention/training, and saved files. Preserve the different stated retention rules for Try On versus De-wrinkle; do not replace them with a generic privacy slogan. Use No previews yet and remove the allowance reassurance from the empty gallery.
steps.limits: Observed unavailable configuration, empty reference, and four preselected garments. Generation, purchase, actual provider processing, and results were not exercised.

steps.name: Closet search
steps.strength: Search field, matching garment, code, and category are direct; results update as you type. No-results copy gives a short recovery instruction without adding a feature pitch.
steps.issue: No material overexplanation in the rendered Closet search result.
steps.accessibility: Keep accessible clear-search and result labels, plus garment codes. VoiceOver navigation not tested.
steps.recommendation: Keep the native search structure; do not trim useful identifying metadata just to reduce label count.

steps.name: Sort & filter
steps.strength: Only Sort and Color appear for All pieces; no tagline or instructional paragraph.
steps.issue: No material copy bloat. Type and closet controls are conditional in source, reducing unused labels.
steps.accessibility: Native labelled rows are clearer than replacing labels with icons.
steps.recommendation: Keep this pattern: one task title, useful field labels, current values, Done.

steps.name: Fits search
steps.strength: No marketing or explanatory text; search and Done are direct.
steps.issue: Two different outfits are both called Untitled fit with only a piece count to distinguish them; the gallery's date fallback and images disappear.
steps.accessibility: Distinct date/name labels would also help users distinguish results without seeing a collage.
steps.recommendation: Use the existing date fallback and a small fit thumbnail. Keep the copy short while making each result identifiable.
